page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-8 is a general-purpose server instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B14 processor, the instance allocates 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core on a dedicated basis. The CPU architecture includes a 32 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, including AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% during stress-ng testing. However, multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench scores align with the middle 50% average. A notable performance tradeoff is observed in memory bandwidth; while cached small-block reads perform at an average level of 565.97 GB/sec, uncached large-block reads and writes fall into the bottom 25% weak category at 37.36 GB/sec and 14.86 GB/sec respectively. Additionally, while the instance handles small 135M parameter LLM inference at average speeds, performance drops significantly to the bottom 10% for medium 7B parameter LLM text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c3d-standard-8 offers a balanced resource profile for standard workloads without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. Given its average database operations, static web serving throughput of 10.45 GB/sec, and standard software compilation capabilities, this instance is suited for general-purpose applications, web serving, light database tasks, and basic serialization workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-8 is a general-purpose server configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor on the x86_64 architecture, it features 4 physical cores, a 32 MB L3 cache, and supports AVX-512 instructions. While stress-ng benchmarks show strong single-core CPU performance in the top 25%, multi-core execution and software compilation scores remain average. A key hardware tradeoff is the lack of local storage and bundled GPUs, alongside weak uncached memory bandwidth. Qualitatively, the instance provides a balanced resource density for standard workloads. It is best suited for general-purpose applications, static web serving, and moderate database operations.
